questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had always dreamed of studying in England because of a fascination with the country, its culture and its customs. I specifically chose Canterbury to see new areas of England, including some beautiful nature spots. Moreover, the university had a lot of different interesting law modules to choose from.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy and I had no issues with it

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of information sent on e-mail, a reception, as well as different apps you could use

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I chose to live in an accommodation with shared kitchen and bathroom. There was also an option to have your own bathroom which cost more

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I did not look into any meal plans but had a shared kitchen in my dorm

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I think it's important to schedule a cleaning regime that everyone in the dorms takes turn on. I would consider getting a dorm room with my own bathroom if that's important and in case you are unlucky with your flatmates (if they do not share your cleaning standards). I would also have liked to know that the kitchens in my dorm - Darwin Houses - all have gas stoves (something I personally struggled with using)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was all quick and easy and happened online via an email

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, there is a reception for all the dorms and all relevant emails are listed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: They had made a mistake with letting me register for two classes that were overlapping so I had to change one of my modules but that process itself was easy and manageable

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, I would make sure that the dorm house is suitable to you. I would also make an effort with finding friends and joining all the many social events right away.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was disappointed with the quality of the law modules. It was not as "concrete" as I am used to and involved a lot of discussions of people's personal opinions (not based on law). Moreover, the director of graduate studies of the university was not very helpful and gave me wrong and misleading information about sourcing on the essays as well as the information you had to provide on the cover sheets of the essays.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the level was a lot lower than I am used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Again, it was not as "concrete" as I am used to and involved a lot of discussions of people's personal opinions (not based on law). I would have liked it to be more to-the-point and factual.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Privacy and Data Protection Law (LAWS9210), and 2) Commercial Credit (LAWS9070)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can only recommend the Privacy and Data Protection Law (LAWS9210). It was the one that gave the biggest academic outcome.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Because I struggled with the gas stove in the dorm kitchen, I did order and buy already-made food more than anticipated

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The dorm is a little expensive for what you get. Everything else was less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a myriad of clubs and activities to choose from - rugby, dancing of various kinds, swimming, tennis, french etc etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My biggest recommendation is to join as many of the welcome week social activities as possible. That is where I found almost all of my friends for the entire stay. Joining a society is of course also a great idea.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking trips to the following places: 1) Rye, 2) Dover, 3) Folkestone, 4) Whistable, 5) Seven Sisters Cliffs, 6) London, and 7) Bath.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy as it is pretty similar to the Danish culture. However, I did miss some of the food from back home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be yourself, be positive and open, and show your curiosity for them! Ask them questions about themselves

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the food

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The extrovertedness, humor, and politeness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Make sure to attend as many events in the welcome week as possible,
2) Make sure that the accommodation is suitable to you,
3) Make sure to sign up for classes that you think you will actually find interesting and useful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was the wonderful people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Lack of proper and nutritious food and my flatmates not sharing my cleaning standard

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
